message.content:
Yes—Atlanta’s local government does have a process for handling noise complaints. Here’s how you can report one: | Step | What to Do | Where to Go | |------|------------|-------------| | **1** | Identify the source & time | Gather details (address, approximate time, description of the noise) | | **2** | Contact the police or city department | • Call 911 if the situation is urgent (e.g., ongoing disturbance, safety concern)
• For non‑emergency complaints, call the Atlanta Police Department’s non‑emergency line at 404‑656‑4000
• Alternatively, use the City of Atlanta’s online “Noise Complaint” portal (available on the official website) | | **3** | File a formal complaint | • If calling, provide your name, phone number, and the details you gathered.
• If filing online, complete the required fields (location, time, nature of the noise, any evidence such as audio recordings). | | **4** | Follow up | The city will typically send a police officer to investigate. You may receive a citation if the noise violates the city’s noise ordinance. | ### Quick Reference * **City of Atlanta Noise Ordinance** – prohibits loud music, barking dogs, construction noise, etc., during certain hours (usually 11 p.m.–7 a.m.). * **Penalties** – first offense: $100 fine; repeat offenses can lead to higher fines or civil action. If you’re unsure whether the activity falls under the ordinance, the police dispatcher can advise you. Reporting helps keep neighborhoods peaceful and ensures that the city enforces its noise regulations fairly.
